holidays.name: National Sugar Cookie Day
holidays.description: A sweet celebration of the humble sugar cookie, the blank canvas of the baking world. Bakers everywhere roll, cut, frost, and sprinkle their way to buttery bliss, usually while sneaking dough off the counter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food holiday that has been popularized by food bloggers and social media. Sugar cookies trace back to 1700s Pennsylvania, where German Protestant settlers in Nazareth made a version of them, and they are often called Nazareth sugar cookies.
holidays.funFact: The sugar cookie was named the official state cookie of California in 2025, and the Nazareth sugar cookie is a historic favorite of Pennsylvania German communities.

holidays.name: National Fried Chicken Day (Observed in Some Calendars)
holidays.description: A crispy, crunchy, golden-brown tribute to one of the world's most beloved comfort foods. Celebrants are encouraged to eat with their hands and to never apologize for the grease on their fingers.
holidays.origin: Fried chicken holidays are a food-calendar tradition in the United States, with the date varying by source. The dish itself blends Scottish frying traditions with West African seasoning techniques, and it was developed in the American South.
holidays.funFact: Scottish immigrants were deep-frying chicken in fat long before it became a Southern staple, while many English cooks of the time preferred to boil or bake their poultry.

holidays.name: Sugar Cookie Day Companion: Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the wisdom of diversifying, whether it's your investments, your snacks, or your egg-carrying strategy. It encourages people to spread out their risks and their omelet ingredients.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance inspired by the proverb, which is often credited to Miguel de Cervantes' 1605 novel Don Quixote, where the idea of not risking everything in one place appears.
holidays.funFact: The proverb is so old that Cervantes used a version of it in Don Quixote in the early 1600s, making it more than 400 years old.

holidays.name: Martyrdom of the Báb
holidays.description: A solemn Bahá'í holy day commemorating the execution of the Báb in 1850 in Tabriz, Persia. Bahá'ís around the world suspend work on this day and gather at noon for readings and prayers.
holidays.origin: The Báb, the herald of the Bahá'í Faith, was executed by firing squad on July 9, 1850. The day is one of nine Bahá'í holy days on which work is suspended.
holidays.funFact: According to Bahá'í accounts, the first attempt to execute the Báb failed when the bullets severed the ropes that suspended him and he was found unharmed in his cell.

holidays.name: Argentina Independence Day
holidays.description: A national holiday in Argentina filled with parades, folk music, flags, and plenty of traditional dishes like locro, a hearty stew. Families often gather for big meals and patriotic celebrations.
holidays.origin: The holiday marks the 1816 declaration of independence from Spain, signed by the Congress of Tucumán on July 9, 1816.
holidays.funFact: The house in San Miguel de Tucumán where independence was declared is now a museum, and the city's famed locro stew is a staple of the day's celebrations.
